commander_identity.mechanical_plan: cEDH interaction commits targeted crimes to pay {1} for Marchesa top-two hand/grave selection; play fast combo plus interactive stack denial and repeatable crime permanents.
commander_identity.natural_ceiling: Bracket 5 cEDH from original October 11 first-place event source; no unmeasured causal win-rate or tournament guarantees.
commander_identity.anti_homogenization: Preserve Marchesa low-cost targeting and top-two selection rather than generic UBR combo alone; retain Alchemist Bow and crime engines.

whole_deck_audit.roles_and_overlaps: Revisited all 99 positions: eleven creature-oriented cEDH denial/utility slots, three combos, fast mana, high-efficiency interaction, paid crimes and direct hand/grave engines. Fixed identity pieces Spatial Binding, Parasite, Spellskite, Lapis, Magda, Tezzeret, Bow; challenged ten distinct incumbent slots.
whole_deck_audit.mana_base_and_curve: 29 actual land faces including one MDFC; 28 front-side lands plus Soporific Springs back. Marsh Flats replaces color-conditional Great Hall; Talon Gates, Urborg, Urza Saga and Ancient Tomb remain utility. Unquantified three-color early-mana stress and life budget disclosed.
whole_deck_audit.interaction_resilience: Retains Force Will Negation, Fierce Guardianship, Mana Drain, Flusterstorm, Pact and Mindbreak Trap; steals creatures with Gilded Drake and stops opponent library searching with Opposition Agent, but cutting Dispel and Minor Misstep has real protection cost.

whole_deck_audit.current_baseline_strength: October 15 locked tournament-derived 100 is already fast cEDH with three independent combos and repeatable crime engines; eight replacements are measured against its opportunity costs rather than a wholesale rebuild.
whole_deck_audit.candidate_pool_scope: Reviewed earlier M5 hypotheses, sealed M6 owner-equivalent Pass C notes, commander-specific EDHREC inclusion, Scryfall text and OFF-RANKED emerging crime cards; no Colab rerun.
whole_deck_audit.off_ranked_search_conclusion: Gilded Drake, Scrabbling Claws, Mayhem Devil, Snuff Out, and Sink MDFC improve meaningful targeted interactions with Marchesa versus standalone engine homogenization.

final_changes.coherent_package_tradeoff: Eight whole-deck upgrades add second Oracle compact line, flash opponent tutor denial, direct ETB and sacrifice crimes, Claws repeatability, free targeted creature removal, flexible blue MDFC and typed dual fetch. Lose two narrow counters, Counterbalance passive tax, costly enchantment copy, sorcery second extra turn, storm treasure ramp, legendary mana filter and Tolaria upkeep trick.

final_candidate.deckwide_reconciliation: Exactly 100 physical cards, 100 distinct names, commander first, 8 exact equal swaps; 29 land faces one MDFC; full fresh Scryfall 100/100 legally UBR; no exceptions.

owner_authority.owner_approval_question: This deck is complete. Do you approve it?

open_ended_optimization_audit.remaining_99_review: After selecting eight, audited every remaining baseline role and challenged retained Magda and Praetor's Grasp specifically. Reviewed full alternative 100s restoring Counterbalance, switching Claws to Talisman, and adding Intuition as a ninth swap. Coherent enemy-search denial, repeatable crime, and color constraints justify exact eight.

post_floor_challenges.tradeoff: Ragavan can produce more immediate combat Treasure but requires an unblocked attack, while Magda is repeatable whenever crimes are committed and preserves the commander-first resource identity.

Intuition is instant-speed targeted crime, but its three card pile hands the adversary selection: with Breach LED Freeze they can strand Breach in a grave that cannot yet be replayed without an enabler.

larger_swap_packages.case_for_extra_swaps: At nine swaps, Intuition on the opponent's end step commits a targeted crime while binning cards toward Underworld Breach; may optimize particular pods with enough graveyard recursion access.
larger_swap_packages.why_not_selected: An opponent picks one of the three cards to hand. With Breach LED Brain Freeze pile, they can put Breach into a graveyard without any independent access to cast it; Grasp remains reliable opponent disruption with double-black cost.

open_ended_optimization_audit.quality_based_stop_reason: The search stopped at eight for strategic reasons, after testing 100-card eight and nine-swap portfolios and challenging two further retained slots: another combo tutor worsens pile reliability, a secondary cheap mana rock removes repeatable targeting, and exchanging Magda erodes commander identity. Remaining alternatives do not clearly improve source-paid three-color access, enemy interaction, or fast win consistency.

low_swap_heightened_audit.off_ranked_opportunities: Reviewed off-ranking new target-crime enablers and cEDH relevant creature theft, graveyard denial and modal land bounce beyond old M5 two-land swaps.

multi_slot_packages.result_and_rationale: The selected eight-card complete 100 retains Claws, Magda and Grasp; stronger target crime turns and grave hate at some copying/timing cost.
Complete alternative 100 with Talisman instead of Claws; BR pips improve but target-player crime and grave hate decrease.
Fully staged nine-swap Intuition candidate adds targeted instant tutoring and graveyard setup, but the opponent controls which card is put in hand; selected Grasp disrupts opponents more reliably.

low_swap_heightened_audit.alternate_cuts_for_prior_holds: Alternative Magda/Counterbalance and Claws/Talisman portfolios were fully constructed, but Magda and Claws stay for repeated own commander payoffs.
low_swap_heightened_audit.strongest_argument_against_baseline: The untouched cEDH list is strong; the baseline Counterbalance, slower four-mana Treasure engine, and second dangerous extra-turn effect make target-driven Marchesa value less immediate.
low_swap_heightened_audit.evidence_based_answer: Eight selected swaps survived full research and opportunity-cost analysis; no multiplayer win-rate improvement asserted.
